questions.q: What is the correct hierarchy in General Ledger?
options: Journal line contains journal entries, which contain batches
Batches and journal entries are the same thing
Journal lines contain batches, which contain journal entries
Journal batch contains journal entries, each of which contains journal lines
questions.explain: The hierarchy is batch, then one or more journal entries, each with one or more lines.

questions.q: Can a single journal batch hold more than one journal entry?
options: No, a batch always holds exactly one journal entry
Only if all entries use the same account combination
Yes, several related journal entries can be grouped in one batch
Only for system-generated sources, never Manual
questions.explain: A batch can hold multiple journal entries, which is why several related accruals can be reviewed and posted together.

questions.q: What is a control total used for?
options: Setting the journal's approval threshold
Self-checking manual entry by comparing an expected total you type in against what was actually entered
Restricting which accounts can be used in a batch
Automatically balancing an unbalanced journal
questions.explain: A control total is an expected-amount field that flags a mismatch before the batch is completed, catching data entry errors early.

questions.q: What does an 'Incomplete' batch or journal status mean?
options: It is still being entered, or it failed validation
It has already posted
It is waiting in an approval workflow
It has been permanently closed
questions.explain: Incomplete means the journal is still being entered or has not yet passed validation.

questions.q: What is one benefit of grouping several related journals into a single batch?
options: It removes the requirement that debits equal credits
It automatically changes their journal category
They can be reviewed, approved, and posted together as one unit
It prevents the batch from ever needing approval
questions.explain: Batching related journals lets them move through review, approval, and posting as a single unit instead of one at a time.
